jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

UC Berkeley’s Office of Strategic Communications leads communications for the No. 1 public university in the world. We tell the Berkeley story to inspire audiences and elevate the distinct narrative of the university's contributions to California and the world. Our mission is to promote the University’s excellence in education, discovery and public service. We provide leadership and services in five integrated functions: News and media relations, executive communications, internal communications, crisis communications, and marketing communications.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of Executive and Internal Communications (Executive Director) serves as a communications advisor and speechwriter for the Chancellor of UC Berkeley. Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Communications, this position is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive executive communications strategy that advances the Chancellor's leadership, supports other Cabinet leaders as needed, strengthens Berkeley’s institutional narrative, and fosters trust with internal and external constituencies.

The Executive Director brings a sophisticated understanding of how language, leadership, and strategy intersect – crafting communications that are precise, authentic, and aligned with the Chancellor's voice and the university's mission across every level of executive engagement, from day-to-day interactions to defining institutional moments.

The Executive Director also supervises and develops a small but growing team, currently including the Director of Executive Communications and the Director of Internal Communications, with additional direct reports anticipated as the function evolves. This role is a member of the Strategic Communications leadership team and plays a key part in building a cohesive and high-performing executive communications function within Strategic Communications.

In close partnership with the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Communications, the Executive Director of Executive and Internal Communications (Executive Director) provides strategic communications counsel and executes a broad portfolio of executive communications on behalf of the Chancellor. This includes primary responsibility for all speechwriting, remarks, talking points, op-eds, social media, and all forms of communications supporting leadership engagement. This role also manages media relations specific to the Chancellor and other key leaders as needed, including triaging and responding to media requests, proactively developing Chancellor-centric visibility and profile opportunities, and advising on the reputational and communications dimensions of issues that directly involve the Chancellor.

The Executive Director develops and maintains a forward-looking executive communications plan that anticipates key moments, manages the Chancellor's speaking and engagement calendar from a communications perspective, and ensures consistency and strategic coherence across all Chancellor-facing communications. This position applies breadth and depth of higher education knowledge to navigate the complex organizational, political, and reputational landscape of a major public research university, and brings a contemporary understanding of how emerging technologies are reshaping executive communications and the stewardship of authentic leadership voice.

The Executive Director works in close coordination with the Chancellor's Office, Strategic Communications, and other senior leaders to ensure the Chancellor is well-prepared, well-positioned, and well-supported across all communications contexts.

This role also leads Berkeley’s internal communications function, developing and implementing a strategic approach to employee and campus community engagement that connects faculty and staff to the university’s mission, strategic priorities and leadership vision. This role also oversees Berkeley’s internal communications channels and editorial calendar, ensuring a regular and strategic cadence of communication that keeps the campus community informed, engaged, and connected to Berkeley’s broader institutional direction. The executive director is comfortable operating at both the strategic and executional level – bringing vision and structure while being willing to roll up their sleeves to get work done.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is: August 24, 2026 For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Develop and execute a comprehensive executive communications plan for the Chancellor that anticipates key moments, aligns with institutional priorities, and ensures strategic coherence across all communications contexts.
Support the Chancellor in the development of remarks, addresses, and presentations — serving as a skilled collaborator and writer who helps translate the Chancellor's own ideas, priorities, and voice into compelling communications for a wide range of audiences and occasions, from major institutional moments to day-to-day engagements
Draft talking points, op-eds, letters, messages to the campus community, video scripts, and other content that reflects the Chancellor's authentic voice and advances institutional priorities.
Manage the Chancellor's speaking and engagement calendar from a communications perspective, assessing, prioritizing, and developing opportunities for executive visibility.
Conduct research and interviews to inform content development, translating complex ideas and institutional priorities into clear, compelling language.
Coordinate with the Office of the Chancellor, Strategic Communications, and other subject matter experts to ensure the Chancellor is well-prepared and well-positioned across all communications contexts.
Apply emerging tools and technologies to the communications development process in ways that enhance the communications process and outcomes.
Proactively develop and pitch leadership visibility opportunities — including news stories, profiles, and thought leadership — that advance UC Berkeley's institutional priorities and reputation.
Manage media relations on behalf of the Chancellor and other executives as needed for institutional-level topics, issues, and priorities where the Chancellor serves as the primary voice and representative of UC Berkeley.
Triage and respond to media requests involving the Chancellor in coordination with the Media Relations office, senior leaders, and other subject matter experts, ensuring the Chancellor is well-prepared and strategically positioned on matters of institutional significance.
Prepare the Chancellor for media engagements by developing comprehensive briefing materials, anticipated questions, and key messages that reflect the full institutional context of the topics at hand.
Develop and maintain relationships with journalists and editors covering higher education, research, and issues of relevance to UC Berkeley and its mission.
Work with the Strategic Communications Issues team to monitor the media landscape for emerging opportunities and threats that may require the Chancellor's engagement as the institution's principal spokesperson.
Work with the Chancellor’s social media team on ensuring quality, engaging content that inspires and engages audiences.
Provide ongoing counsel on the reputational and communications dimensions of emerging issues and pending decisions that are likely to require the Chancellor's direct engagement.
Implement a strategic internal communications framework that connects faculty, staff, and students to the university's mission, priorities, and leadership vision - ensuring a regular and strategic cadence of communication that keeps the campus community informed and engaged.
Developing proactive and responsive strategies that help the campus community navigate complex, sensitive, and high-stakes moments – from institutional change to national events that reverberate on campus.
Serve as a strategic advisor to campus communicators across schools, colleges, and units - establishing best practices, developing shared frameworks and tools, and building a more coordinated approach to internal communications across the institution.
Provide supervision for the Executive Communications and Internal Communications team members, ensuring work is aligned with the Office of Strategic Communications' priorities. and supporting growth and development of the team..
Directly supervise employees by assigning work, establishing priorities, monitoring performance, and ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality communications.
Coach, mentor, and develop staff by establishing performance expectations, providing ongoing feedback, conducting performance evaluations, and supporting professional growth in accordance with university policies.
Foster collaboration across executive communications, internal communications, media relations, and other Strategic Communications functions to ensure coordinated planning, consistent messaging, and effective execution.

jobs.title: TFS Director of Development
jobs.description:
Tsuru for Solidarity (TFS)'s Director of Development position leads development work at the organization, with a mix of individual giving, fundraising events, corporate and foundation grants. 

About Us:

Tsuru for Solidarity’s mission is to educate, advocate, and protest to close all detention sites; build solidarity with other communities of color that have experienced forced removal, detention, deportation, separation of families, and other forms of racial and state violence; coordinate intergenerational, cross-community healing circles addressing the trauma of our shared histories.

Tsuru for Solidarity is a member and fiscally sponsored project of Asian Americans for Civil Rights and Equality (AACRE), a network dedicated to long-term movement building and social justice infrastructure. An employee hired for this role will be an employee of AACRE.

Position Description

Tsuru for Solidarity (TFS) seeks a Director of Development to lead the development work of the organization. This position will be supervised by the TFS Executive Director and will work closely with the Leadership Council (board) as well as the fundraising committee. Regular participation in virtual meetings typically scheduled Mondays-Fridays from 12pm-5pm Eastern time is required. Travel to TFS events, about 20% of time, is required. Some evening and weekend work is also required.

Key Responsibilities

Lead annual giving campaign

Design and oversee the organization’s annual fundraising campaign, including setting fundraising goals, developing campaign messaging and timelines, tracking performance, and analyzing results to refine the campaign year over year.

Develop and steward donor network

Build and strengthen relationships with individual donors, create and implement a donor stewardship plan, and maintain regular communications, recognition, and donor engagement.

Lead fundraising events including from individual donors and corporate sponsors

Plan, coordinate, and deliver fundraising events that engage both individual donors and corporate sponsors. Manage event logistics, sponsorship packages, attendee experience, and post event follow-ups.

Prospect, write, and administer foundation grants

Research and identify new foundation funding opportunities aligned with TFS goals and priorities, draft grant proposals and letters of inquiries, and manage the full grant lifecycle including deadlines, compliance, reporting, and maintaining funder relationships.

Strategic thought partner to Executive Director, Directors, and Leadership Council on development

Collaborate and partner closely with the Executive Director, Directors, and Leadership Council to shape the overall TFS development strategy. Provide recommendations on donor cultivation, campaign planning, and revenue growth.

Additional duties as needed in support of TFS development

Support in operational improvements, special projects, and other priorities as they arise.

Required Qualifications

Excellent communication, interpersonal, and strategic planning skills
Ability to work both collaboratively and independently. 
A minimum of five years experience in development, operations or non-profit leadership. 
Strong intercultural, multigenerational, and interpersonal communication skills. 
Familiarity with and understanding of Japanese American incarceration history, anti-racist movements, immigrant rights, abolitionist organizing, and healing justice 

Preferred Qualifications

Additional experience in communications or operations 
Any multilingual skills (Spanish, Creole, Japanese)

To Apply

Apply by submitting an application and uploading a cover letter, resume, and an optional writing sample through the AACRE Careers page or to: https://bit.ly/TFSDevDirector

In your cover letter, describe your interest in the position and the organization, and highlight relevant experience. Please note that incomplete applications that do not contain a cover letter and resume may not be considered.

AACRE is dedicated to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable work environment where everyone is valued and discrimination has no place. We are committed to serving the rich diversity of Asian American and Pacific Islander communities, and strongly encourage women, trans and gender expansive individuals, people of color, immigrants, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and those living with disabilities to apply.

AACRE is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). We consider all qualified candidates for employment regardless of age, race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, national origin, immigration status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, arrests or conviction records, or veteran status.

We are committed to supporting our employees to thrive in service of our mission by providing generous benefits, which include 100% health, dental, vision, life and long-term disability insurance for employee coverage and 65% for dependent coverage; employer-funded health reimbursement account; and paid time off.

Please visit https://aacre.org and https://tsuruforsolidarity.org/ for more information.

, Togetherness

Develop relationships with donors and prospects to solicit and close gifts in support of USC Athletics

Manage a portfolio of 150 to 200 current and potential donors.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will possess a bachelor’s degree and a minimum of five years of experience. Combined experience/education as substitute for minimum experience.

Description

Job Title : Executive Director - Confidential Developmental Services

Location: New York, NY

FLSA Status : Full Time – Exempt

Supervisory Responsibilities: Yes X No

Position Summary: Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for the strategic leadership, direction, programmatic quality, financial integrity, management, operations, and overall sustainability of the Developmental Center. The CEO oversees all agency programs, operations, finances, facilities, and personnel while ensuring excellence in service delivery, regulatory compliance, organizational culture, and mission impact. The CEO serves as the organization’s strategic leader, representative, and primary public advocate, while ensuring high-quality educational and developmental outcomes for children and families, workforce stability, strong internal systems, and operational accountability.

The CEO should possess substantial expertise in preschool special education, developmental disabilities services, multidisciplinary educational staffing models, and highly regulated school-based operations.

The role requires a leader with demonstrated experience managing complex educational and human service environments, including facilities oversight and capital construction / renovation projects. The CEO will lead and work closely with an executive team composed of the Chief Program Officer (CPO), Chief Finance Officer (CFO), Senior Director of Workforce Innovation and Director of Operations and Finance.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership & Strategy

Provide strategic leadership and organizational direction aligned with the agency’s mission, values, and long-term sustainability.
Lead strategic planning efforts that anticipate policy, regulatory, demographic, and funding changes affecting preschool special education and developmental disability services.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Partner closely with the Board of Directors to support governance, strategic oversight, and public advocacy.
Drive organizational innovation and growth by identifying opportunities to expand services, strengthen community partnerships, and enhance long-term organizational impact.

Programmatic & Educational Oversight

Oversee all preschool special education, related service, and developmental disability programs to ensure high-quality educational, therapeutic, and developmental outcomes.
Ensure compliance with all NYSED, NYSDOL, NYCDOE, DOHMH, and other applicable regulatory and contractual requirements.
Maintain expertise in multidisciplinary staffing structures and operational requirements for special education environments, including teachers, therapists, psychologists, nurses, paraprofessionals, and related providers.
Oversee program census, classroom utilization, staffing models, and operational performance across all educational and program sites.
Ensure ongoing program evaluation, quality improvement, and implementation of best practices in early childhood special education.

Workforce Development & Talent Strategy

Provide strategic oversight of workforce development initiatives designed to train unemployed and underemployed adults as certified special education teacher assistants and teachers.
Develop workforce partnerships that strengthen recruitment pipelines and address staffing shortages in special education and related service professions.
Lead agency-wide talent strategy, succession planning, recruitment, retention, and leadership development efforts.
Ensure strong human resource practices, performance management systems, and professional development structures across the organization.
Oversee the sourcing and stewardship of public and private funds for workforce initiatives.

Financial, Operational & Facilities Management

Ensure the organization’s long-term financial health through sound fiscal management, operational planning, and resource allocation.
Oversee audits, financial reporting, risk management, adoption of emerging technologies including AI, and compliance activities in coordination with finance staff and external partners.
Direct agency-wide facilities operations, infrastructure planning, maintenance, and regulatory compliance across multiple sites.
Lead capital improvement, renovation, and construction initiatives in collaboration with architects, engineers, contractors, and regulatory agencies.
Ensure construction and facilities projects are completed within budget, on schedule, and with minimal disruption to educational and therapeutic operations.

Fundraising, External Relations & Advocacy

Partner with the Board and development team to strengthen philanthropic, governmental, and corporate fundraising efforts.

The Division of Transportation Planning & Management (TPM) is responsible for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods on the City's streets, supporting the larger goals of economic and social vitality for people living, working and doing business in New York City. The Traffic Engineering & Planning (TEP) unit, within TPM, is responsible for conducting, reviewing, and approving transportation engineering and planning studies, analyses and methodologies.

Founded in 2001 by breast cancer survivor Lydia Dody, Hope Lives! provides compassionate, no-cost
supportive services to individuals in active treatment for breast cancer in Larimer and Weld counties. Through partnerships with healthcare providers and more than fifty community service providers, Hope Lives! helps address the physical, emotional, social, and financial challenges that can accompany treatment and recovery.

For more than 25 years, Hope Lives! has built a trusted reputation in the community. Today, the organization is entering its next chapter with an engaged Board of Directors, a strong network of supporters and partners, and a clear commitment to thoughtful, sustainable growth.

The Opportunity

Hope Lives! is seeking an Executive Director who can build upon a respected legacy while helping shape the organization’s future. This is a hands-on executive leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable being visible in the community, cultivating donors, leading fundraising efforts, managing staff and volunteers, overseeing major events, and ensuring strong day-to-day operations.

The Board has identified six priorities that will define success in this role: public leadership, fundraising growth, relationship development, operational and staff leadership, event success, and focused organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a highly visible, relationship-oriented leader who combines strategic thinking with a willingness to remain actively engaged in the day-to-day realities of a growing nonprofit. They will understand that fundraising is fundamentally about relationships, that community visibility drives opportunity, and that organizational growth must be supported by strong systems, responsible stewardship, and an exceptional team. The ideal Executive Director leads with integrity, humility, accountability, sound judgment, and genuine compassion for the individuals and families Hope Lives! serves.

What Success Looks Like

Serve as the public face of Hope Lives!, increasing awareness and representing the organization with professionalism, compassion, and credibility throughout Northern Colorado.
Drive fundraising and philanthropic growth through individual giving, major gifts, sponsorships, grants, donor stewardship, and new revenue opportunities.

Provide effective day-to-day leadership for the organization, including staff and volunteer management, budgeting, compliance, program oversight, and operational accountability.

Guide thoughtful organizational growth by strengthening systems, expanding community impact, diversifying revenue, and positioning Hope Lives! for long-term sustainability.

Identify opportunities to improve organizational systems, strengthen financial sustainability, expand community impact, and support long-term growth.

This full-time position is based at FIRC's new building in Breckenridge, CO. The role requires weekday work and a steady in-office presence, generally Monday through Thursday, balanced with regular travel across the county for community meetings, site visits, and evening or weekend commitments as needed. In-person leadership in the community is just as vital to this role as is its visibility throughout Summit County. 

Core Responsibilities 

1. Strategic Leadership & Community Advocacy 

Lead the implementation and ongoing evolution of FIRC's strategic plan in response to the community's shifting needs. 

Serve as the primary champion for key community issues, including food equity and housing stabilization, healthcare navigation, parenting support, and mental health resources. 
Facilitate FIRC's role as a neutral, trusted convener in Summit County, building coalitions with regional nonprofits, local officials, and food and health networks to coordinate services and expand shared funding opportunities. 

2. Diversified Fund Development & External Relations 

Partner with the Board and the Philanthropy and Communications Director to design and execute a comprehensive revenue strategy to support the $6-$7 million operating budget. 

Personally lead the engagement, cultivation, and direct solicitation of major individual donors, corporate partners, and institutional foundations. 

Act as the primary ambassador for FIRC, effectively communicating its impact to the media, public officials, philanthropic networks, and community stakeholders. 

Build and maintain relationships with local, state, and federal government representatives. 

Represent FIRC on relevant external boards, coalitions, or advisory groups that raise the organization's profile and strengthen community ties. 

3. Fiscal Stewardship & Operational Oversight 

Partner with Finance leadership to maintain rigorous fiscal controls, ensure audit readiness, and implement forward-looking financial strategies to protect organizational sustainability. 

Provide high-level oversight of FIRC’s social programs, food bank, and thrift store operations, maximizing both community impact and earned revenue. 

Maintain a transparent, productive partnership with the Board of Directors, equipping them with the data and insight needed for strong governance. 

4. People, Culture & Equity Leadership 

Supervise, coach, and support senior leadership team members, fostering a culture of professional growth, clear accountability, and high staff retention. 

Model and champion FIRC’s collaborative, transparent, and input-oriented workplace culture across all staff members. 

Ensure a deep institutional commitment to advancing cultural competency, language justice, and equity within both internal operations and external service delivery. 

Qualifications And Experience 

College degree required. A Master's degree in Social Work, Public Policy, Nonprofit Organizational Management, or a related field is preferred. Candidates without an advanced degree who have comparable experience in a related field will also be considered. 

Minimum of 5 years of senior organizational leadership experience, ideally within a non-profit human services sector or community resource center of similar scale. 

Demonstrated success in securing and growing philanthropic support through foundations, corporations, government grants, and comfort in solicitation of major gifts, and individual donor cultivation. 

Experience operationalizing big ideas, managing complex multi-million-dollar budgets, and applying forward-thinking strategies for nonprofit revenue growth. 
Familiarity with local public policy mechanics, coalition-building, and navigating complex community dynamics as a neutral convener. 

A proven history of building highly motivated, cohesive teams, reducing turnover, and leading with an open, collaborative style. 

Deep commitment to the stability and wellbeing of Summit County's workforce and residents, with an understanding of the wraparound human services model. 

Candidates may be subject to a background check post-offer of employment 

Preferred Attributes

The compensation for this role is anticipated to range from $160,000 to $185,000 per year, commensurate with experience. FIRC offers a competitive benefits package, including: 

Five weeks of paid time off per year (flexible and fixed), and additional personal time off as well as paid holidays. Time off accrual rate increases with tenure.

Local recreation discounts and perks

Summary

Position Type: Full-time, exempt, salaried supervisor role.
Scope of Role:
Manages state level operations, overseeing a state, a portion of a state, or multiple states.
Typically, responsible for regions producing $30 million or more in annual revenue.

Key Responsibilities:
Operational Management: Oversees service delivery and ensures alignment with state-level goals.
Strategic Leadership: Drives strategic planning, vision, growth, and development initiatives.
Financial Oversight: Manages financial performance, profitability, and budgetary compliance.
Human Resources: Supervises recruitment, retention, training, and management of state-level staff.
Regulatory Compliance: Ensures adherence to licensing requirements and regulatory standards.
Quality Improvement: Implements strategies to enhance service quality and meet organizational benchmarks.
Stakeholder Relations: Builds relationships with stakeholders, families, guardians, and external partners.
Advocacy and Lobbying: Represents the organization in public policy efforts and lobbying activities

Essential Job Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below.

Services And Supports

Quality Improvement: Oversees implementation of quality improvement standards and practices; works with the Quality Improvement Director and directs the Quality Improvement Manager in developing and implementing state strategies to manage and improve quality.
Compliance: Implements state licensing and compliance strategy; Reviews and responds accordingly to regulatory correspondence, including correction orders and monitors state compliance.
Customer Service: Implements strategies to maintain and foster positive relationships with individuals receiving services, families, guardians, case managers and funders; and implements state improvement plans in response to satisfaction survey results as appropriate; implements stakeholder communication plan.
Incident Management: Oversees implementation of Sevita incident management protocol; manages timely incident reporting and response to incidents; reviews trends; implements proactive strategies to reduce or eliminate serious incidents across the state; directs state team to address safety concerns, limiting the potential for continued concern or incident.
Management of Individuals’ Assets: Implements system to assure protection of individual’s funds and property, assuring safety and accuracy.
General Health Care: Oversees implementation of health and safety programs, medication administration and dietary planning; identifies and assures implementation of strategies to limit illness or serious incident; oversees healthcare documentation; supervises Director of Nursing, as applicable.

Stakeholder Relations

Public Relations: Manages relations and communications concerning the general community, neighbors, government, competitors, and other outside organizations.
Payer and Government Relations: Maintains and fosters relations with state and regional government authorities and referral agencies such as counties, regional centers, managed care contractors, and government administrators.
Related Organizations: Participates in advocacy on behalf of individuals served or supported; joins and takes a leadership role in state trade associations on committees and boards of directors.
Political Involvement: Develops and implements public policy strategy; participates in building relationships with legislators and government officials; makes political contacts and lobbies or advocates on behalf of the industry, company and individuals receiving services.

Personnel

Management: Oversees implementation of human resource practices including recruitment, retention, training, scheduling, record keeping and management of employees; conducts monthly meetings with state-level employees including Regional Directors, Business Manager, Quality Improvement Manager, Human Resources Manager, and other personnel.
Recruitment and Hiring: Collaborates with HR Business Partners and the Talent Acquisition teams on state hiring strategy and needs. Meets with Talent Acquisition Manager weekly to address hiring needs. Recruits, hires, and interviews Regional Directors. Consults with the Regional Director and Talent Acquisitions team on hiring of Area Directors. Makes hiring decisions on RDs and state functional leaders in partnership with Vice-president of Operations.
Coaching, Discipline and Termination: Oversees and implements Sevita employment practices; conducts annual evaluations for state team and oversees state evaluation process for all employees; in consultation with human resource personnel, reviews written warnings and approves all involuntary terminations for state level personnel.
Training: Organizes and oversees orientation and training programs; contributes to the design of training materials, creates addendums for state requirements; coaches and develops training facilitation skills of direct reports.
Employee Safety: Directs workers’ compensation return to work implementation.

Growth And Development

Planning: Oversees strategic and blueprint planning to grow state business; incorporates growth and budgetary planning; reviews best practices for dissemination across the state; maintains a healthy and productive business showing year over year growth.
Development: Directs operations personnel in efforts to grow revenue maintain margin and meet state growth plans; encourages state and regional development to serve new populations and drive geographic and service line expansion; encourages and approves new start or other core development initiatives.
Scouting: Promotes relationships with payers, competition, and other stakeholders; identifies opportunities by following industry trends, responding to payer need and requests for proposal.
Acquisition: Identifies potential candidates for tuck-in or acquisition; assists with diligence and integration planning; assumes management of acquired entities.
Efficiency: Directs state strategy to increase census, maintain occupancy, improve daily attendance, and maximize utilization.

Financial Management

Management: Responsible for the financial performance of the business units, reviews financial statements, reviews purchasing, and manages system to assure billing compliance and documentation.
Spending: Responsible for state-wide budget and forecast; monitors purchasing to maintain budgetary compliance; monitors staffing and spending; submits proposals for capital improvement.
Compensation: Works with the Vice President, Operations to develop and implement fair and equitable wage plans; approves wage status changes for state team and according to wage guidelines and budgetary parameters.
Eligibility & Authorizations: Ensures effective and efficient oversight of key process dates and timely completion of redeterminations / renewals where applicable to maintain clean billing

Census Management

Marketing: Coordinates with marketing to define state's marketing strategy and priorities (i.e., collateral, social media, branding, success stories, etc.).
Referrals: Approves referral closures to validate that thorough and critical decision- making processes are applied to every referral. Conducts retrospectives on closed referrals where service expansion opportunities or other strategic program changes would support future admissions.
Census Performance: Monitors census and referral dashboards, reviewing progress against census targets, analyzing admissions, discharges, and leave days trends, and ensuring timely and proactive response and thorough placement decision making; identifies and oversees corrective plans to address census challenges in the state and supports Regional Directors with implementation of regionally-based action plans and coordination with other parts of the business (Finance, Talent Acquisition, Marketing, IT, etc.) as needed.

Maintenance

Maintenance and Repair: Oversees state environmental safety planning; develops longer term plans for capital improvement.
Environment: Implements and monitors strategies to assure neat, clean, and safe residential and vocational environments, including grounds.

Founded in 2001 by breast cancer survivor Lydia Dody, Hope Lives! provides compassionate, no-cost
supportive services to individuals in active treatment for breast cancer in Larimer and Weld counties. Through partnerships with healthcare providers and more than fifty community service providers, Hope Lives! helps address the physical, emotional, social, and financial challenges that can accompany treatment and recovery.

For more than 25 years, Hope Lives! has built a trusted reputation in the community. Today, the organization is entering its next chapter with an engaged Board of Directors, a strong network of supporters and partners, and a clear commitment to thoughtful, sustainable growth.

The Opportunity

Hope Lives! is seeking an Executive Director who can build upon a respected legacy while helping shape the organization’s future. This is a hands-on executive leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable being visible in the community, cultivating donors, leading fundraising efforts, managing staff and volunteers, overseeing major events, and ensuring strong day-to-day operations.

The Board has identified six priorities that will define success in this role: public leadership, fundraising growth, relationship development, operational and staff leadership, event success, and focused organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a highly visible, relationship-oriented leader who combines strategic thinking with a willingness to remain actively engaged in the day-to-day realities of a growing nonprofit. They will understand that fundraising is fundamentally about relationships, that community visibility drives opportunity, and that organizational growth must be supported by strong systems, responsible stewardship, and an exceptional team. The ideal Executive Director leads with integrity, humility, accountability, sound judgment, and genuine compassion for the individuals and families Hope Lives! serves.

What Success Looks Like

Serve as the public face of Hope Lives!, increasing awareness and representing the organization with professionalism, compassion, and credibility throughout Northern Colorado.
Drive fundraising and philanthropic growth through individual giving, major gifts, sponsorships, grants, donor stewardship, and new revenue opportunities.
Build and strengthen meaningful relationships with donors, healthcare providers, sponsors, volunteers, foundations, nonprofit partners, businesses, and community leaders.
Provide effective day-to-day leadership for the organization, including staff and volunteer management, budgeting, compliance, program oversight, and operational accountability.
Lead the planning and successful execution of signature events, including the Annual Gala, Golfing for Hope, Walk for Hope, and future fundraising initiatives.
Guide thoughtful organizational growth by strengthening systems, expanding community impact, diversifying revenue, and positioning Hope Lives! for long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute an annual fundraising plan aligned with Board-approved goals and organizational priorities.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward donors, sponsors, foundations, and community partners while expanding Hope Lives!’ philanthropic reach.
Serve as the organization’s primary ambassador and spokesperson at community events, healthcare functions, civic organizations, media opportunities, and public engagements.
Strengthen relationships with physicians, oncology practices, hospitals, imaging centers, healthcare providers, nonprofit organizations, and referral partners.
Provide strategic leadership and hands-on management for Hope Lives!’ signature fundraising events, including event plans, budgets, timelines, committees, sponsors, volunteers, vendors, logistics, guest experience, and post-event evaluation.
Lead and support staff and volunteers, establishing clear expectations, accountability, collaboration, and opportunities for development.
Oversee Hope Lives! programs and service delivery, including provider relationships, program utilization, outcomes, documentation, and grant reporting.
Prepare and manage the annual operating budget in collaboration with the Board Treasurer and provide timely, accurate financial information to the Board.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, reporting requirements, bylaws, Board policies, and sound nonprofit governance practices.
Provide strategic oversight for marketing, communications, public relations, social media, website
content, newsletters, and organizational storytelling.
Partner with the Board of Directors to implement strategic priorities and provide operational insight, data, and recommendations that inform future planning. Identify opportunities to improve organizational systems, strengthen financial sustainability, expand community impact, and support long-term growth.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, healthcare administration, public administration, communications, marketing, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant leadership experience.
• Minimum of five years of progressively responsible nonprofit, healthcare, charitable, or mission-driven leadership experience.
• Demonstrated success in fundraising, donor cultivation, sponsorship development, grants, or other
revenue-generating initiatives.
• Experience managing budgets and demonstrating sound financial stewardship.
• Experience supervising staff and working effectively with volunteers.
• Experience working collaboratively with a Board of Directors or governing body.
• Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, presentation, and public-speaking skills.
• Strong technology skills with demonstrated ability to effectively use and learn CRM, bookkeeping, donor management, event, and other business software platforms.
• Strong organizational, strategic planning, relationship-building, and problem-solving abilities.

Preferred qualifications include experience in healthcare, patient advocacy, oncology, breast cancer support, or human services; a CFRE or comparable credential; and established relationships within Northern Colorado’s nonprofit, healthcare, philanthropic, or business communities.

Compensation & Growth Opportunity

Starting Salary Range: $75,000–$80,000 annually, depending on qualifications and experience.
Performance & Salary Growth: The Executive Director will be eligible for performance-based salary growth up to approximately $92,000 based on sustained progress toward the organization’s financial growth, fundraising, and sustainability goals. In addition, the Executive Director will be eligible for an annual performance bonus upon achievement of financial goals established by the Board through the annual strategic planning and budgeting process.

The Board intends to periodically review Executive Director compensation as Hope Lives! grows to ensure alignment with organizational performance, financial sustainability, market competitiveness, and the expanding scope of the role.

Benefits include a flexible work environment, health benefits, paid time off, and opportunities for professional development, subject to current organizational policies and benefit plans.

Why Hope Lives!?

This is an opportunity to do more than maintain an organization. It is an opportunity to help build its next chapter. Hope Lives! currently operates with an annual budget of approximately $350,000, and the Board has established a long-term aspiration to grow the organization toward $750,000 to $1 million in annual revenue while preserving the compassionate, client-centered culture that has defined Hope Lives! since its founding.

The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to expand community awareness, strengthen
philanthropy, deepen strategic partnerships, build organizational capacity, and increase the number of
individuals and families supported throughout Northern Colorado. For a mission-driven leader energized by relationships, fundraising, community engagement, and thoughtful growth, Hope Lives! offers the opportunity to create lasting impact.

How to Apply

Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter, résumé, and three professional references to the Hope Lives! Executive Director Search Committee at Mark@HopeLives.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Hope Lives! is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive environment for all
employees, volunteers, clients, and community partners. Employment decisions are made without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

About The Family & Intercultural Resource Center (FIRC) 

Since 1993, FIRC has worked to ensure that everyone can create and maintain a life in Summit County, Colorado. As the county's only nonprofit social services agency, FIRC provides wraparound services that help one in three residents afford healthy food and housing, navigate healthcare challenges, and build the connections and stability they need to thrive. By filling these gaps, FIRC supports the workforce that keeps this vibrant mountain community running and strengthens the diversity that makes Summit County feel like home. 

About The Role

The Executive Director’s primary responsibility is to maintain FIRC as a strong, sustainable, and well-regarded resource to the Summit County community. Specifically, the Executive Director is responsible for: 

Ensuring that FIRC makes consistent progress toward achieving the organization’s strategic goals and overall mission, while upholding its core values, 

Fundraising with a focus on major gifts from individual and institutional donors, 

Leading advocacy efforts, building community partnerships, and facilitating FIRC’s role as a neutral convener for the Summit County community, 

Managing the organization's operations, finances, and staff 

The Executive Director leads all FIRC functions (Finance, Development, Operations, and Programs), managing an annual budget of $6-$7 million and a staff of 30-32. The head of each function reports directly to the Executive Director. This position reports to the FIRC Board of Directors, which conducts the Executive Director's annual performance review. 

This full-time position is based at FIRC's new building in Breckenridge, CO. The role requires weekday work and a steady in-office presence, generally Monday through Thursday, balanced with regular travel across the county for community meetings, site visits, and evening or weekend commitments as needed. In-person leadership in the community is just as vital to this role as is its visibility throughout Summit County. 

Core Responsibilities 

1. Strategic Leadership & Community Advocacy 

Lead the implementation and ongoing evolution of FIRC's strategic plan in response to the community's shifting needs. 

Serve as the primary champion for key community issues, including food equity and housing stabilization, healthcare navigation, parenting support, and mental health resources. 
Facilitate FIRC's role as a neutral, trusted convener in Summit County, building coalitions with regional nonprofits, local officials, and food and health networks to coordinate services and expand shared funding opportunities. 

2. Diversified Fund Development & External Relations 

Partner with the Board and the Philanthropy and Communications Director to design and execute a comprehensive revenue strategy to support the $6-$7 million operating budget. 

Personally lead the engagement, cultivation, and direct solicitation of major individual donors, corporate partners, and institutional foundations. 

Act as the primary ambassador for FIRC, effectively communicating its impact to the media, public officials, philanthropic networks, and community stakeholders. 

Build and maintain relationships with local, state, and federal government representatives. 

Represent FIRC on relevant external boards, coalitions, or advisory groups that raise the organization's profile and strengthen community ties. 

3. Fiscal Stewardship & Operational Oversight 

Partner with Finance leadership to maintain rigorous fiscal controls, ensure audit readiness, and implement forward-looking financial strategies to protect organizational sustainability. 

Provide high-level oversight of FIRC’s social programs, food bank, and thrift store operations, maximizing both community impact and earned revenue. 

Maintain a transparent, productive partnership with the Board of Directors, equipping them with the data and insight needed for strong governance. 

4. People, Culture & Equity Leadership 

Supervise, coach, and support senior leadership team members, fostering a culture of professional growth, clear accountability, and high staff retention. 

Model and champion FIRC’s collaborative, transparent, and input-oriented workplace culture across all staff members. 

Ensure a deep institutional commitment to advancing cultural competency, language justice, and equity within both internal operations and external service delivery. 

Qualifications And Experience 

College degree required. A Master's degree in Social Work, Public Policy, Nonprofit Organizational Management, or a related field is preferred. Candidates without an advanced degree who have comparable experience in a related field will also be considered. 

Minimum of 5 years of senior organizational leadership experience, ideally within a non-profit human services sector or community resource center of similar scale. 

Demonstrated success in securing and growing philanthropic support through foundations, corporations, government grants, and comfort in solicitation of major gifts, and individual donor cultivation. 

Experience operationalizing big ideas, managing complex multi-million-dollar budgets, and applying forward-thinking strategies for nonprofit revenue growth. 
Familiarity with local public policy mechanics, coalition-building, and navigating complex community dynamics as a neutral convener. 

A proven history of building highly motivated, cohesive teams, reducing turnover, and leading with an open, collaborative style. 

Deep commitment to the stability and wellbeing of Summit County's workforce and residents, with an understanding of the wraparound human services model. 

Candidates may be subject to a background check post-offer of employment 

Preferred Attributes 

Bilingual Capability:
 Professional proficiency in Spanish is highly preferred to support cultural integration and diverse community demographics. 

Compensation And Benefits 

The compensation for this role is anticipated to range from $160,000 to $185,000 per year, commensurate with experience. FIRC offers a competitive benefits package, including: 

Five weeks of paid time off per year (flexible and fixed), and additional personal time off as well as paid holidays. Time off accrual rate increases with tenure. 

Medical, dental, and vision insurance with employer contribution for employees and eligible dependents (some plans are covered 100% by employer, multiple buy-up options available) 

Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for health and dependent care expenses. 

Life Insurance and AD&D, covered by employer 

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and mental wellness support 

Short- and Long-Term Disability (STD, LTD)

403(b) Retirement plan, with up to 3% employer match 

Paid training and professional development opportunities 

Discounted ski passes and access to shared ski medallion 

Local recreation discounts and perks
